content: <thought>We have the molecular ion at m/z 127.0997, which likely corresponds to [M+H]⁺, giving a neutral exact mass of ≈ 126.09 Da. The 13C NMR shows seven distinct carbon signals: 161.4 ppm (ester carbonyl), 143.9 ppm and 130.3 ppm (conjugated alkene carbons), and four aliphatic sp³ carbons at 26.7, 22.8, 21.4 and 19.2 ppm. This pattern suggests a C₇ molecule containing an ester carbonyl attached to a conjugated C=C system and a short alkyl chain. A formula that fits the mass and contains one carbonyl and one C=C is C₇H₁₀O₂ (exact mass 126.068 Da, [M+H]⁺ 127.075 Da), which is consistent with the observed m/z within experimental tolerance. The most plausible structure is methyl 3‑buten‑2‑oate (methyl crotonate), which has the required carbonyl (≈ 161 ppm), two alkene carbons (≈ 144 and 130 ppm), and four aliphatic carbons (the methyl of the ester and the three carbons of the butenyl chain). The SMILES for methyl crotonate is **C=C(C)C(=O)OC**. I will validate this SMILES and then provide it as the final answer.
